races.name: Newgrange Hotel Handicap

runners_data.name: Thurso
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner here; Sam Coen gets a clean lead on good-to-firm going where he ran a career-best (1st/6f/Firm), and if allowed to bowl along uncontested on this flat 6f this is his optimum scenario — though OR=72 and 34 days since last run are worth noting against sharp rivals.

runners_data.name: Phoenix Pairc
runners_data.note: W J Lee aboard a genuine hold-up horse who won at 7f on good/soft and has placed at OR higher than today's mark; the drop to 6f is a query but good-to-firm is fine, and a true gallop is needed for him to land his finishing run from the back.

runners_data.name: Poweracclaim
runners_data.note: Ben Coen partners a consistent prominent racer whose best recent efforts have come at 6f on good ground — four of his last five runs at this trip in similar conditions, and the JP Murtagh yard is firing (2/22 in 14 days), making this a live each-way candidate from a tracking position.

runners_data.name: In The Gloaming
runners_data.note: Gary Carroll rides a lightly-raced 3yo who is a genuine hold-up type stepping back down from 7f; limited good-ground evidence (1/3) but the form is respectable, and a genuinely run 6f on fast ground could unlock improvement for this Oliver-trained youngster.

runners_data.name: Aurora Nova
runners_data.note: A seven-year-old hold-up performer who has shown ability at this trip on good ground (two wins at 6f) but recent efforts have been modest and OR=64 represents his current ceiling — Wesley Joyce (3) claiming five pounds helps, though consistent finishing positions in double figures are a concern.

runners_data.name: Are You In Or Out
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who landed a 6f handicap on good ground ten days ago and is clearly in form; Nicola Burns claims five pounds for the Conor Maxwell yard (1/3 in 14 days), and the quick turnaround plus wide draw need watching, but she is versatile enough to handle a tactical race.

runners_data.name: Gotta Catch'em All
runners_data.note: Genuine prominent-running type who races over a shorter trip than her recent hurdling form suggests — her sprint handicap experience is dated and she is unlikely to secure her natural early position with so many prominent rivals in this field, which meaningfully compromises her chance.

runners_data.name: Irish Rumour
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes over on a horse who has placed four times in his last ten outings at 6-7f on good ground; a consistent prominent performer who is likely to find a spot just behind the front rank, and DBM's tactical nous makes him a horse to keep on the right side.

runners_data.name: Coincidental Glory
runners_data.note: Declan McDonogh partners a 3yo prominent type who has placed at 6f on good ground and whose trainer Adrian McGuinness is in excellent form (3/27 in 14 days); has run respectably at this trip on similar going and looks the type to emerge from the chasing pack if the pace is fair.

runners_data.name: Reinforce
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer who has been competing predominantly at 5f and drops back to that trip in recent runs — 6f may ask questions of her finishing speed, and OR=58 with a modest recent record (form: 6908-0) make it hard to see where the win comes from on this card.

runners_data.name: Elly Bay
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who was second at 7f on good ground and ran a tidy fifth at 5f/6f recently; James Ryan takes the ride and a step back to 6f with only 127lbs looks manageable, but the 10-day turnaround and tendency to hover around mid-field placings make her better suited as a place candidate.

runners_data.name: Verified
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type who carries a notable flag for fading in the finish — recent form on 5f good ground is very poor (form: 9-0002), and OR=56 is the lowest of the hold-up contingent; will need things to go perfectly and a genuine pace to make any impact here.

runners_data.name: Prime Sign
runners_data.note: True hold-up type pushed into a midfield position on the map; the fades-in-finish flag and a run record of 12/18/5/24/6 in the last five underline the inconsistency, and with OR=55 and 29 days off, hard to construct a winning scenario even if pace develops as hoped.

runners_data.name: The Cosy Corner
runners_data.note: A 2yo last season who has not raced for 317 days — Chris Hayes takes the ride for the in-form Gavin Cromwell yard (4/34 in 14 days), and freshness may be a positive, but the long absence, all below-average finishes, and fades-in-finish flag make this very much a wild card on return.

runners_data.name: Dubai Opulence
runners_data.note: Young 3yo hold-up performer whose form figures (13/15/9/8 on good and similar) suggest she has yet to find her feet in handicap company; the fades-in-finish tag and lowest OR in the field at 50 make it very difficult to make a case, even with the claiming allowance factored in.

runners_data.name: Step Back In Time
runners_data.note: An 8yo veteran with a natural prominent style who is unable to secure his favoured early position in this deep field and is redistributed to midfield — form at 6f on good ground has been poor recently (11/9/14/12) and OR=44 leaves him with very little room for error.

races.paceDynamic: Thurso is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 16-runner field and, critically, is unlikely to be seriously pressured for the lead, giving Sam Coen the luxury of controlling the tempo from the front on good-to-firm ground. Behind him, a clutch of genuine prominent types — Poweracclaim, Irish Rumour, Coincidental Glory, Are You In Or Out, and Elly Bay — will compete hard for the early positions just off the pace, creating a compact and competitive first furlong without necessarily torching the gallop. The field contains more prominent-running horses than the race shape can accommodate: Gotta Catch'em All and Step Back In Time are true prominent types who are likely to find themselves racing further back than ideal, unable to secure their natural berth with so many rivals ahead of them. With one horse dictating a sustainable, uncontested gallop on a flat 6f track in good-to-firm conditions, this shape sets up most favourably for horses who can race prominently in behind Thurso and produce a sustained late challenge — pure hold-up closers will face a stiff task if the pace is not truly true.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Thurso Controls, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Thurso dictates a steady-to-fair gallop and the prominent horses track him at a realistic pace throughout.
scenarios.body: Thurso sets a rhythm that suits those sitting second or third, and with no rivals able to dislodge him, the first two or three home come from the chasing group who get a clear tow into the straight. Poweracclaim, Irish Rumour, and Coincidental Glory are best placed to pounce on Thurso from a prime tracking position on a flat, straight 6f.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Sweep Late
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group push the pace harder than expected in the early stages, burning off their reserves before the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A genuine gallop stretches the field and creates a gap at the back end that suits true hold-up horses swooping from the rear. Phoenix Pairc and In The Gloaming, both genuine hold-up types with fine-ground credentials, are most likely to benefit as they arrive late in an honest-run dash.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Runner Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack check each other without pressing Thurso, turning the race into a false-run, slow-tempo affair.
scenarios.body: Thurso, uncontested and allowed to lob along, simply outkicks everything in the final furlong with his rider never having to pick up the reins hard. This scenario rewards Thurso's ability to control tempo absolutely, with Are You In Or Out potentially the best of the rest if she can hustle up close enough from her wide draw.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Disrupt
scenarios.trigger: If Gotta Catch'em All or Step Back In Time force their way into prominent positions and inject unexpected early pace.
scenarios.body: The scramble for position in the first couple of furlongs creates a messy, uneven gallop that suits neither the front-runners nor the closers uniformly. Irish Rumour, who has tactical versatility and honest recent form, is best equipped to adapt mid-race, while Coincidental Glory may also profit from the chaos if her trainer's strong recent form (3/27 in 14 days) translates.

watchPoints.text: Watch for Thurso's early lead being uncontested — if Sam Coen gets a clear, unchallenged front, the whole race shape shifts in favour of horses tracking him at close quarters (Poweracclaim, Irish Rumour), and the hold-up horses may find the final-furlong gap simply too wide to bridge.

Monitor the draw and early position of Gotta Catch'em All and Step Back In Time in the first furlong — if either manages to force their way prominently despite being redistributed, they could inject an unexpectedly sharp early gallop that disrupts the tempo and unsettles the genuine holders behind.

The Cosy Corner returns after 317 days for Gavin Cromwell (4/34 in 14 days) — trainer form is live enough to take seriously, but a juvenile returning from such a layoff in a 16-runner sprint on fast ground is a genuine market mover to watch rather than trust blindly.

Are You In Or Out ran just 10 days ago and takes a quick return; if she bounces or fails to reproduce her winning form, it removes one of the few genuine in-form prominent types from contention and strengthens the case for Coincidental Glory and Poweracclaim to fill the space behind Thurso.

Good-to-firm conditions are confirmed for this race — any horse in the field whose sim-going record shows poor strike-rate on fast ground (notably Phoenix Pairc at 0W1P in 6/9 good-ground runs and Aurora Nova at 2W4P in 12/15) should be treated with some caution if conditions firm up further during the afternoon.

races.name: Navan Adventure Centre Handicap

runners_data.name: All Hail
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed pace-setter here; wins this role by default but carries a notable fading pattern in finishes and has not won in four starts, so holding on once headed is the key question — her OR of 69 is the highest in the race and she handles this going.|

runners_data.name: The Right One
runners_data.note: Won most recently over 5f on Soft and has strong place form over this exact trip on Good ground; Ronan Whelan is a booking worth noting and the handicap mark of 67 looks workable if she reproduces her best.|

runners_data.name: White Smoke
runners_data.note: True hold-up type who ran just 8 days ago; the 7lb claimer Sadhbh Tormey rides, and with limited place form on Good ground and a short 5f trip, getting competitive from the rear is a tall ask here.|

runners_data.name: Amerilis
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with place form over 6f on Good, dropping to 5f here which is a query — tongue-tie fitted and she has shown consistency without winning; Donagh O'Connor a capable pilot if she travels well early.|

runners_data.name: Lumiere Des Etoile
runners_data.note: 61 days off the track and has registered zero wins or places on Good going in recent starts; dropping back to 5f from longer trips and the layoff combine to make this a challenging assignment.|

runners_data.name: Cashel Blue
runners_data.note: Won over course and distance (5f, Good) most recently and that C&D form is the most relevant single piece of evidence in this race; W J Lee takes over in the saddle and K J Condon's yard has shown a pulse recently.|

runners_data.name: Boston Max
runners_data.note: In-form sprinter with two recent wins, but his natural style is prominent and he has been pushed into a midfield mapping because of the crowded pace picture — racing out of his preferred position tempers his chance even with the form in his favour.|

runners_data.name: Love Bomb
runners_data.note: Visor-wearing hold-up horse carrying a fade flag; recent form figures of 047080 tell a bleak story and the Good to Firm ground has not yielded a place in seven relevant starts — hard to make a case for.|

runners_data.name: Mini Cotai
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse by style mapped forward due to the crowded rear; Wesley Joyce's 3lb claim helps at the weights, but nine outings without a win and limited form at the sharp 5f trip make this tough.|

runners_data.name: Another Nice'day
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up type shifted to midfield on the map, carrying a fade warning and the lowest OR in the field at 42; 7lb claimer Orla Tynan rides and the form figures on Good ground offer no encouragement.|

races.paceDynamic: All Hail is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will control the tempo from the gates on Good to Firm ground over this sharp 5f at Navan — creating a sustainable, uncontested gallop rather than a race run at a frenetic pace. The Right One, Amerilis, and Cashel Blue will press prominently behind, with Cashel Blue's recent course-and-distance win at this track over 5f on Good ground making her a particularly dangerous stalker. This field holds more genuinely front-running and prominent types than the map can accommodate at the head of affairs — Boston Max is a true prominent racer who is redistributed to midfield, and Another Nice'day and Mini Cotai are true hold-up horses pushed forward on the map; All Hail and Cashel Blue are most likely to actually secure the positions that define this race shape. A controlled, single-pace gallop on fast ground over a short trip strongly favours prominent racers who can track the leader and pounce in the final furlong — hold-up horses face too short a race to mount a meaningful late challenge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If All Hail sets a steady, uncontested pace and the prominent trackers close efficiently in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: All Hail dictates a measured tempo, leaving the prominent stalkers with enough energy to reel her in or pass her close home on the fast ground. Cashel Blue and The Right One, both proven at 5f on Good going, are ideally placed to pounce from just off the lead.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If All Hail's uncontested lead proves decisive and no prominent horse can close the gap in time.
scenarios.body: With no horse pressuring All Hail early, she banks energy through the race and may simply have too much in reserve for anything to catch her over this short trip. Her going form is solid on this surface and a lone leader in a small pace field can be very hard to reel in.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Scramble, Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If the pace unexpectedly quickens early and prominent horses string the field out, leaving redistributed types floundering.
scenarios.body: Boston Max, forced out of his natural prominent role, may find himself racing at an unfamiliar rhythm and struggle to produce his best. A pace collapse or unusually fast early fractions could create a chaotic final furlong where a lightly-exposed type finds a gap.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and the front two or three tie each other up, gifting ground to rear runners.
scenarios.body: This scenario depends on hold-up horses like White Smoke or Lumiere Des Etoile, who face the double disadvantage of a short trip and a race likely run at a controlled tempo — the conditions rarely favour late closers over 5f on Good to Firm ground.

watchPoints.text: Cashel Blue is the most dangerous horse in the race — C&D winner on identical going, and if she tracks All Hail cleanly she is the most likely to overhaul the pace-setter in the final furlong.

All Hail's fade flag is a genuine concern; watch whether she begins to stop once headed, because any hesitation in the final 1f could gift the race to the stalkers even if she has led for much of the race.

Boston Max's redistribution out of his natural prominent position means punters should watch his early behaviour in the stalls and his position leaving the gates — if he gets up close to the pace naturally, his two recent wins make him a live danger.

The Right One's headgear (p — probably a hood or similar) and Ronan Whelan's booking combine as a stable signal worth monitoring; her 5f place form on Good ground is the strongest in the field behind Cashel Blue.

Good to Firm conditions are confirmed for this race despite the headline going listed as Good — the faster surface will compress finishing kicks and further reduce the prospects of White Smoke, Lumiere Des Etoile, and the other genuine hold-up types.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Race

runners_data.name: Confused
runners_data.note: Trained by Mrs John Harrington and likely to use her front-running style to command this race from the front; two runs on similar going both saw her placed and she steps up in trip to 1m2f which may suit, though at 40 days off she needs to have trained on.

runners_data.name: South Island
runners_data.note: Donnacha Aidan O'Brien-trained three-year-old who is 0W0P from five runs on similar going, so the form profile is modest, but a prominent style means she can at least get involved tactically; the step back to 1m2f from 10f trips is not a major concern but the consistency question is real.

runners_data.name: Summer Is Tomorrow
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent racer by nature, though pushed into a midfield slot on the map because multiple horses are chasing the same early positions; Dylan Browne McMonagle rides and the visor headgear is noted, but eight runs on similar going have returned only one win and three placings, so the form ceiling may be limited.

runners_data.name: Hard Promises
runners_data.note: The major unknown in the race — just one career start to her name (third over 10f on Soft) and a lofty OR of 120 shared with Confused, so she carries a significant upside if that rating is warranted; Ben Coen is an excellent pilot and A Oliver's string is in decent nick at 3/15 over 14 days, making her impossible to dismiss despite the experience deficit.

runners_data.name: Mo Mhuirin
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery trains and rides this mare himself, which is a notable angle; a natural prominent type re-positioned at the rear of the map purely to fill that role, she won over 8f on Standard and placed twice over 10f on Good, so the trip and going are fine, but she will likely push forward early rather than settle as a true hold-up horse.

races.paceDynamic: Confused is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only five runners over 1m2f on Good to Firm ground at Navan, she is likely to stride into a comfortable, uncontested lead from the outset and control tempo from her own rhythm. South Island and Summer Is Tomorrow are both genuine prominent types who will seek to track the leader, but with multiple horses wanting that same position the early stages may see some jostling for the first bend before Confused asserts her natural role. Hard Promises is unknown in terms of style, while Mo Mhuirin has been redistributed to hold-up purely to balance the map — she is a true prominent type likely to push forward rather than settle at the rear. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural positions; Confused is most likely to lead, with South Island best placed to lock in second, while Summer Is Tomorrow and Mo Mhuirin may end up slightly further back than ideal. This race shape — a controlled, sustainable gallop set by one horse — strongly favours horses that can track the pace and pick up efficiently in the straight, rewarding the prominent racer with the best turn of foot rather than those requiring a truly searching test.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Confused Controls, Prominent Striker
scenarios.trigger: If Confused dictates an honest but uncontested pace and the race is decided by who picks up best in the straight.
scenarios.body: Confused leads throughout at a tempo she sets herself, and the horse tracking most comfortably into the straight delivers the decisive move; a sustainable gallop suits a well-positioned tracker over a finisher requiring maximum pace pressure.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Confused sets a very slow early pace that bunches the field and the race becomes a sprint finish from 2f out.
scenarios.body: A dawdling gallop compresses the field and turns the race into a tactical sprint, negating Confused's front-running advantage and allowing any horse with a sharp turn of foot to overhaul her late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Outsider Gate-Crashes
scenarios.trigger: If Hard Promises, whose style is unknown but whose OR of 120 matches Confused, travels powerfully and produces a decisive late burst.
scenarios.body: Hard Promises, lightly raced and holding an official rating equal to Confused, is an unknown quantity that could prove well above average; if Ben Coen delivers her late on a pace-honest gallop she has the class to sweep past.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Storm Home
scenarios.trigger: If early pressure from multiple prominent types creates a genuinely fast pace that leaves the front rank empty-tanked entering the straight.
scenarios.body: Mo Mhuirin and Summer Is Tomorrow, though neither is a true hold-up horse, would benefit if the early scrap for position between Confused, South Island and others burns out the leaders and leaves a gap to close into; this is a low-probability shape given the field's collective tendency to race prominently.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether South Island challenges Confused for the lead early — if she pressures rather than tracks, the pace dynamic shifts and the race becomes genuinely contested rather than a controlled lead.

Hard Promises is a significant watch on debut angles: a single run on Soft tells us almost nothing about her ceiling on Good to Firm, and a jockey/trainer combination in form means she could be priced longer than her true chance warrants.

Monitor Mo Mhuirin in the market — trainer-jockey combination, a win already on the board this season, and a natural inclination to race prominently mean she could be sharper off 40 days than her mapped position suggests.

Summer Is Tomorrow's visor headgear is worth noting as a potential switch-on factor for a horse with a patchy record; if the headgear produces a more focused early effort she may secure a better position than the map implies.

races.name: Navan Handicap

runners_data.name: Sonoran
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for G M Lyons on a going that suits (OK on good), but four sim-going runs yield no win and only two places — needs a strongly run race and pace collapse to land from off the pace here.

runners_data.name: Beauparc
runners_data.note: Nicola Burns (5lb claim) partners this veteran stayer who has a course win on turf and placed twice at 12f — long-distance profile is well matched, though his soft-ground form figures more prominently in the hist than his good-ground returns.

runners_data.name: Steel Cut
runners_data.note: Confirmed pace-setter and sole front-runner in the field, giving him uncontested lead; however, his style tag carries a 0.93 fit discount — the horse has shown prominent rather than truly dominant front-running form, and one win/place from three sim-going runs is modest.

runners_data.name: Genoah
runners_data.note: Won twice at 10-12f on standard going with hood and tongue-tie combination, last ran 14 days ago and is race-fit; prominent style is a natural fit for an uncontested-pace shape and his two Naas wins on similar trips are the key formbook entry.

runners_data.name: Daonethatgotaway
runners_data.note: 99-day absence is a flag despite a win and two places at 12f on standard ground — Mark Fahey's 14-day strike-rate is modest and the long layoff tempers confidence, but his prominent style and staying profile are tactically correct for this shape.

runners_data.name: Cala Bonita
runners_data.note: Four-year-old by Matthew J Smith with a win and place at 10f on standard, lightly raced on turf/good ground — prominent style suits, and only 40 days off means fitness is intact; the 0.93 style-fit note reflects this horse could press Steel Cut rather than comfortably sit second, which may be a positive or a risk depending on early pace.

runners_data.name: Lady Chartwell
runners_data.note: In truth a hold-up mover by style, pushed into a midfield slot on the map because the rear of the field is congested — five consecutive poor runs including three finishes of 11th or worse make it hard to make a case regardless of position.

runners_data.name: Letiza
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up operator whose last run was 231 days ago — the lengthy absence is the primary concern; has won and placed on good going at 10f so the conditions are not wrong, but Adrian Nicholls' 14-day figures show no recent runners and race-fitness is uncertain.

runners_data.name: Raydamann
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's runner carries a strong trainer strike-rate (12/64 in 14 days) and has won at 18f on good ground, so stamina is not an issue — his true inclination is to race prominently but is mapped to midfield due to field congestion; the style-fit tag (0.92) reflects he may not secure the prominent berth his form demands.

runners_data.name: Felix Somary
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up type with a fade-in-finish flag; has been running at 6-8f over hurdles and on the flat — stepping up to 1m2f on turf good-to-firm is a major unknown and the distance profile looks stretched based on all available form.

runners_data.name: Admiral Will Brown
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old for Daniel McLoughlin with four consecutive 7th or worse finishes — a true hold-up type pushed into midfield by field congestion, 54 days since last run, and a 0.90 style-fit discount combine to make this the hardest horse in the field to make a case for.

races.paceDynamic: Steel Cut is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will control tempo from the outset at a sustainable gallop on this flat 1m2f Navan track. The good-to-firm surface will keep fractions honest rather than dawdling, but with a single pace-setter dictating an uncontested rhythm, this shapes up as a controlled, single-file race where the front is never truly pressured. That dynamic historically favours prominent and handy types who travel within the pace rather than deep hold-up horses who need a true test to close — Genoah, Cala Bonita and Daonethatgotaway are the profiles most suited to this shape. The field contains more prominent and hold-up types than the race structure can accommodate: Raydamann, Letiza and Lady Chartwell are genuine front-runners or prominent movers by inclination but are mapped to midfield — Raydamann and Cala Bonita are most likely to actually press Steel Cut if they jump well, while the others will find themselves further back than ideal.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steel Cut Controls, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Steel Cut leads uncontested and sets a measured tempo that brings prominent trackers into play from 2f out.
scenarios.body: Steel Cut sets a comfortable, sustainable gallop and the race resolves in the straight as the closest pursuers — Genoah and Cala Bonita — pick off the leader without needing a sprint finish that eludes them.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Lifts, Closers Stay On
scenarios.trigger: If Raydamann or Cala Bonita push up to challenge Steel Cut early, lifting the gallop and setting up a true staying test.
scenarios.body: A more honest pace drains the prominent types in the final furlong, allowing hold-up horses who travel smoothly through the race to close late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Slow Burn, Late Surge Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Steel Cut crawls and the entire field bunches into a sprint finish off a falsely run race.
scenarios.body: With no meaningful tempo, the race becomes a flat-out 2f dash and a horse with tactical speed and a fresh turn of foot outsprints the field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Steel Cut's trainer has this horse primed for a bold front-running display and no rival has the early speed to close the gap.
scenarios.body: Steel Cut builds an unassailable lead with a strong gallop and simply outstays the field, with the prominent trackers unable to close.

watchPoints.text: Steel Cut's gallop sets the entire race tempo — if Sam Coen (5lb claim) misjudges the pace in the early furlongs and goes too slow, the race collapses into a sprint that Steel Cut may not win; watch the opening 2f closely.

Raydamann (Gordon Elliott, Chris Hayes) is mapped to midfield but is a natural front-runner by inclination — if Hayes pushes up early to secure a prominent pitch, it transforms the pace picture and could lift the gallop to suit closers.

Letiza's 231-day absence is the longest in the field by a wide margin — if fitness is absent, she will drop away rapidly from the 3f pole and block the run of hold-up horses trying to close through the pack.

Beauparc (Nicola Burns 5lb claim) has placed at 12f on good going and the trip is career-proven — watch whether the claim overturns a weight concern and whether he is foot-perfect early from his midfield draw, as his staying profile benefits from being handy.

Felix Somary's fade-in-finish flag combined with a trip extension from 6-8f to 1m2f on turf is a combination that rarely ends well — his position late in the race may impede genuine closers and he is worth monitoring as a potential traffic risk in the straight.

races.name: Navan Racing Festival 14th & 15th November Handicap (0-60)

runners_data.name: Rising Sky
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner — has winning form on good ground over 10f and goes here off a short 8-day turnaround; the tb headgear is noted and Patrick McGettigan (5lb claimer) keeps weight competitive, but the STYLE_FIT flag suggests the mapped prominent role may not reflect natural tendency to lead.|

runners_data.name: Arch Enemy
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up type who has been off 105 days and has a tendency to fade in the finish; most recent form on heavy ground at Leopardstown/Dundalk is hard to trust on this good-to-firm surface and the long layoff is a clear concern.|

runners_data.name: Deuteronomy
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a genuine win and place record on good ground — won over 10f at Dundalk on the Flat and returned 5th here at Navan 23 days ago; the blinkers are on and Nicola Burns claiming 5lbs makes this competitive, with 2W4P in similar going a solid platform.|

runners_data.name: Jazz Forever
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse who fades in the finish — hood worn and recent form shows a string of mid-to-rear finishes over further distances on good and soft; unlikely to get the pace scenario needed over this shorter 1m2f trip and the fade flag is a genuine concern.|

runners_data.name: Robot Rock
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a fade flag who has been well beaten in recent Navan runs including 16th last time out over this exact trip; the tongue strap is noted but a sim-going record of 0W0P gives little encouragement on this surface.|

runners_data.name: Autocrat
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up specialist whose trainer P Sweeney has 0 wins from 4 runners in the last 14 days — showing here in a midfield slot only because the field is overloaded with closers; a true rear-runner competing for ground in a race unlikely to produce the strong pace he needs, and the STYLE_FIT discount applies.|

runners_data.name: Trishuli River
runners_data.note: Prominent racer whose last three runs feature placings at Sligo and Dundalk on standard ground; the tongue and pad headgear combination is noted and this trip suits, though a sim-going return of 0W0P at this level tempers enthusiasm.|

runners_data.name: Cleopatra's Needle
runners_data.note: Interesting hold-up type for H Rogers with Chris Hayes booked — has won at 16f and placed at 8f and 10f on good ground and is the most versatile profile in the field; the sim-going record of 2W6P is the strongest in the race and she brings strong each-way claims from a handy position.|

runners_data.name: Thegooseiscooked
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old prominent-style runner whose recent form shows 13th and 13th but earlier in the season finished 4th and 6th at similar level on good; Rory Cleary is a solid booking and the horse has won on good ground previously, though the most recent efforts suggest a horse on the downgrade.|

runners_data.name: Retro Gal
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up type for Henry De Bromhead — has been beaten in a string of 7ths and 8ths in similar company and the sim-going record of 0W0P from just two good-ground runs is uninspiring; the 10-day turnaround and blinkers first time are headgear angles to note but this is a tough task.|

runners_data.name: Copper Craft
runners_data.note: A confirmed hold-up runner whose natural race position is at the rear — shown here in midfield only because of field overcrowding at the back; Gary Carroll is a reliable booking and there are placings on standard ground in the recent past, but the STYLE_FIT flag is a genuine check on expectations.|

runners_data.name: One For Teigan
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a fade flag and a recent form string of zeros — Wesley Joyce claims 3lbs but the horse has not troubled the judge in any of its last five starts across soft and standard going, and being mapped away from its natural hold-up position further diminishes already weak prospects.|

runners_data.name: Haughty
runners_data.note: Six-year-old true hold-up runner whose last run was 69 days ago — a long absence combined with a sim-going record of 1W1P at this level and the redistribution away from the rear of the field makes Killian Leonard's task a difficult one; won at 7f on standard at Dundalk but that form looks some way removed from this contest.|

runners_data.name: Gold Dublooms
runners_data.note: Four-year-old closer with a fade flag and a tongue strap — has 0W1P in sim-going and recent form shows a 9th last time out at this trip; mapped to midfield due to overcrowding at the rear and the STYLE_FIT flag is pertinent, as this horse is unlikely to produce the finishing run its natural style demands here.|

races.paceDynamic: Rising Sky is the confirmed front runner here and, with only Deuteronomy and Trishuli River likely to push for early prominent positions alongside, the pace is unlikely to be truly searching on good-to-firm ground over 1m2f at Navan. Rising Sky can bowl along at a controlled tempo, dictating the fractions from the front and making this a test of finishing quality rather than raw stamina. The field contains a heavy concentration of hold-up types — Autocrat, One For Teigan, Copper Craft, Haughty and Gold Dublooms are all genuine closers redistributed into a midfield map position simply because there are more hold-up horses than the shape can accommodate at the rear; Cleopatra's Needle and Retro Gal round out the hold-up cluster. In a race where one horse controls the tempo unchallenged and the closers are numerous but competing for the same ground, the tactical verdict is clear: horses racing prominently in the slipstream of Rising Sky — Deuteronomy and Cleopatra's Needle primarily — are best placed to pounce, while the true hold-up horses face a congested finishing straight and a pace that may not be strong enough to fully suit their finishing kick.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Rising Sky Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Rising Sky secures the lead unopposed and sets a controlled, even tempo throughout the 1m2f trip.
scenarios.body: Rising Sky rolls along in front, the field strings out at a steady pace, and those settled just off the leader — Deuteronomy and Cleopatra's Needle — have the prime position to strike when the race quickens entering the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Grind It Out
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just honest enough that the front two or three fade only marginally, leaving prominent-racing hold-up types unable to close.
scenarios.body: Deuteronomy and Cleopatra's Needle, tracking the early pace, find the sprint to the line plays to their style as no closer can generate a winning run from further back.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Rising Sky sets a genuinely strong enough gallop that the prominent horses are cooked turning in, giving true closers a gap to exploit.
scenarios.body: Autocrat or Copper Craft, both genuine hold-up horses who have been redistributed but whose real style is a late run, would need this pace scenario to find room and arrive late; the STYLE_FIT flags on both are a genuine discount to this shape delivering.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Pace, Bunched Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses mid-race, causing a congested sprint finish where positional luck and a clear run decide the outcome.
scenarios.body: With so many hold-up types unable to get back to their preferred spot, a slow-run race turns into a sprint where a horse like Thegooseiscooked or Trishuli River, with a clear run from a handy position, benefits.

watchPoints.text: Rising Sky and jockey Patrick McGettigan — if the 5lb claimer allows the pace to become truly crawling in the early furlongs, the entire race dynamic shifts against the hold-up horses and turns this into a sprint, dramatically compressing the field.

Cleopatra's Needle is the most dangerous horse in the race from a going and form angle — Chris Hayes is likely to push forward earlier than her hold-up tag suggests and she has multiple wins on good ground; watch for her to take a prominent position that her redistribution note understates.

Autocrat, Copper Craft, One For Teigan, Haughty and Gold Dublooms are all genuine hold-up horses competing for the same late ground — if they are all finishing together in a bunched straight, traffic and interference become a live risk that could compromise several runners simultaneously.

Deuteronomy wears blinkers and has Nicola Burns claiming 5lbs — if the horse gets a soft lead to track in second or third, its 2W4P record in similar going makes it the standout beneficiary of the pace shape Rising Sky is likely to create.

Jazz Forever and Robot Rock both carry fade flags over distances that exceed today's 1m2f — both could be more competitive at this shorter trip than their recent form over 13-16f implies, and are worth monitoring in the early stages to see if the shorter distance produces a more prominent early position.
